name: SLRE
listed_description: Super Light Regular Expression library; a small implementation of a subset of Perl regex syntax.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README, docs/overview.md and the repo contain no benchmark; docs only say compiled x86 code is about 5kB and that libraries like PCRE are too heavy for embedded use (a size and footprint claim, no numbers against PCRE for speed). Two web searches found no third-party shootout including SLRE. License is GPL-2.0 or commercial (Cesanta CLA). Last commit 2026-08-26 (docs fixes).

name: spy
listed_description: A C++17 constexpr library for detecting OS, compiler, architecture, and SIMD at compile time.
reason: Not a performance library: compile-time detection of compiler, OS, architecture and SIMD extensions replacing #ifdef chains. No benchmark directory, no performance numbers, no baseline in README or repo. The listing description is stale (README now says C++20, BSL-1.0, 168 stars).

name: st_tree
listed_description: A fast and flexible c++ template class for tree data structures.
reason: Only a directional claim. README and wiki say all operations are logarithmic in node depth except deep copy, and the design page lists complexity goals; no timings, no benchmark directory, no comparison against std::map or any other container. Apache-2.0, 121 stars.

name: std-simd
listed_description: A portable implementation of std::experimental::simd for C++.
reason: No numbers published in the repo. benchmarks/ holds micro-benchmark sources (divides, hypot, rounding, shifts, sincos, run.sh, bench.h printing speedup and cycles per call versus the scalar abi) but no recorded results; README has only a code example. Repo says development moved to GCC libstdc++ and std::simd for C++26. A GNU Radio talk (events.gnuradio.org, seen as a search snippet only, host blocked) reportedly gives scalar vs simd FLOP per cycle on an Intel Xeon W-2145 with GCC 13, but it measures the libstdc++ implementation and could not be opened. Companion repo mattkretz/simd-benchmarks (opened) also has no results. BSD-3-Clause, 655 stars.

name: StrTk
listed_description: A C++ library consisting of high performance string processing routines.
reason: Repo carries comparison source (strtk_tokenizer_cmp.cpp: StrTk tokenizer and split vs Boost tokenizer and split, int and double to string and back vs sprintf, lexical_cast, Karma, atoi, Qi) but no published numbers; README only says extremely fast conversions. The numbers presumably sit on https://www.partow.net/programming/strtk/index.html and code.google.com/p/strtk, both blocked by egress policy (EGRESS_BLOCKED). Two searches found no third-party shootout including StrTk (Boost.Convert's performance page does not list it). MIT, 143 stars.
